B_my_best_attempt_to_overturn_and_why_it.attack: The 'scale' leg of the verdict (Sionna 0.52 dB vs measured 5.2 dB) is measured on the INCOHERENT sum, which is phase-blind by construction and therefore smooth by construction. The observable a detection receiver actually integrates is the COHERENT channel h. If Sionna's coherent channel has azimuth structure of the measured size, the '1/10 of measured' headline dies.

the_number_that_would_have_killed_it.reads: 12.7-15.7 dB span, 6.6-8.2 dB std - LARGER than Das's measured eps of 5.2-5.3 dB. On its face this destroys the scale argument.

why_it_is_not_quotable.reads: |h|^2 grows as N^0.44-0.52 in the number of ray samples - 25.0 dB of drift across a 256x spp ladder at R=1 m - while Sum|a|^2 moves 0.15 dB. The coherent sum of SAMPLED diffuse paths is a divergent Monte-Carlo estimator (each sample carries amplitude ~ sqrt(Omega) ~ 1/sqrt(N), so Sum|a|^2 converges but |Sum a e^{-j phi}|^2 does not). Its azimuth spread is estimator variance dressed as physics, not sigma(az).
why_it_is_not_quotable.verdict_on_the_attack: FAILED. And it fails in the direction that makes Sionna worse: its ONLY converged target observable is the flat one.

second_attack_projected_area.attack: maybe Sionna's flat azimuth envelope is an artifact of one badly chosen scattering coefficient S (the previous auditor listed S as unaudited).
second_attack_projected_area.what_I_found: report15['materials']['by_group'] - production S = 0.2 (plastic body/canopy/prop/gear), 0.3 (carbon arm), 0.0 (ITU metal motor + camera).
second_attack_projected_area.why_it_does_not_help_sionna: (i) S is a pure level knob: jones_mat = sqrt(f_s*Omega)*Gamma*xpd, so S rescales the diffuse channel without touching its shape in azimuth; (ii) the shape comes from f_s, a Degli-Esposti empirical lobe in LOCAL incidence/scatter angles with no wavelength and no object size in it, so no value of S can manufacture target-scale lobes; (iii) worse for Sionna: the two METAL groups (motor, camera) have S = 0 exactly, so in Sionna the strongest scatterers on the airframe contribute NOTHING to the diffuse channel and appear only in the specular channel, which is alive at 1 of 36 aspects.
second_attack_projected_area.what_stays_unknown: whether S=0.2 gives the right ABSOLUTE diffuse level is still not audited (rt_no_rcs_verify B_sphere_S shows a 15.8 dB swing from S=0.2 to S=1.0 on a PEC sphere). I did not close that. Unknown.

third_attack_elevation.attack: the axis is sigma(azimuth AND elevation). The verdict only argued azimuth. Sionna's elevation dependence might be large and real.
third_attack_elevation.reads: Sionna's elevation dependence is enormous - 46.9/55.6/65.6 dB from el=15 to el=0 at R=1/3/10 m - and it is entirely the size-blind specular mirror switching on: at 10/hot the coherent |h|^2 median is -59.653 dB and report15's specular_census records the same cell's specular amplitude as -59.657 dB. That channel's range law is -19.91 dB/decade (1/R^2), not -40 (1/R^4).
third_attack_elevation.verdict_on_the_attack: FAILED, and again in the wrong direction for Sionna: adding elevation to the axis makes PathSolver's angle dependence a binary, size-blind, wrong-range-law cliff rather than a lobe pattern.

fourth_attack_fine_azimuth.the_open_hole_I_inherited: no Sionna azimuth sweep finer than 30 deg exists in any ledger. I re-scanned outputs/ and confirm this: the finest are facet_count (12 az x 30 deg) and report15 (8 az x 45 deg in the census, 3 az in the phase grid).

independent_replication_on_a_second_dron.src: report15 grid.blocks, matrice4e, prod, spp 2.048e9, 5 seeds x 64 rotor phases
independent_replication_on_a_second_dron.reads: 1.72-2.45 dB span, 0.91-1.25 dB std on matrice4e, versus 1.28 dB / 0.52 dB on mavic4pro in facet_count. Two drones, three ranges, two independent scripts: same answer.

realisation_noise_bound.reads: the converged channel repeats to 0.03 dB (median) / 0.43 dB (worst) across seeds, so any structure hiding between 30 deg samples would have to exceed that - and there is no lambda-scale term in the expression that could produce it (a_p = pattern x Jones x lambda/(4 pi L), f_s a function of local angles only).

what_I_can_bound_instead.status: the hole is narrowed by an argument from the verified equations plus a 0.43 dB reproducibility bound, NOT closed by a fine sweep. A 1-2 deg Sionna azimuth sweep is still the clean way to shut it.

C_things_the_verdict_overstates_that_sho.item: 'our PO span 24.37 dB vs Sionna 1.28 dB' in the head-to-head cell
C_things_the_verdict_overstates_that_sho.problem: the 24.37 dB is carried entirely by one point: az=0 PO = -38.018 dBsm, a deep null where our own two kernels disagree by 19.84 dB (SBR gives -18.177 there). Drop az=0 and PO's span over the remaining three azimuths is 3.339 dB - BELOW SBR's 4.408 dB and only 2.6x Sionna's 1.281 dB.
C_things_the_verdict_overstates_that_sho.restate_as: the head-to-head cell shows ours moves 3-4 dB where Sionna moves 1.3 dB, over a 4-point quadrant of one drone. The load-bearing evidence for the axis is the 360-deg grid (p90-p10 9.2-15.7 dB over 45 cuts) and the eps-vs-Das comparison, not this cell.

C_things_the_verdict_overstates_that_sho.problem: validate_measured_airframe's own eps_reading says our azimuth statistics are the wrong distribution family (ours: gamma/gamma/lognormal; measured: Rician with K <= -10 dB, i.e. Rayleigh) and the wrong band trend (measured is flat 5.2-5.3 dB across all three bands; ours is 4.48/3.97/6.48). The ledger's own sentence: 'a real airframe behaves like a rich, stationary scattering ensemble across the band, and ours does not.'
C_things_the_verdict_overstates_that_sho.restate_as: one scalar (the azimuth spread) lands within -1.3/+1.2 dB of the measured value at all three bands. Its band trend and its distribution family do not match. That is still an order of magnitude closer than Sionna's 0.5-1.2 dB, but it is a single-scalar match, not a pattern match.
0.5-1.2 dB, across two drones and three ranges (mavic4pro quadrant 0.52; matrice4e az 0/45/90 0.91-1.25).

D_where_this_axis_actually_stands_after_.the_one_sentence: PathSolver's only converged target observable has 1.3-2.5 dB of azimuth structure and no size, curvature or aperture term anywhere in the expression that produces it; our kernel produces a 360-deg sigma(az,el) whose spread lands within 1.3 dB of the only measured airframe we have. Detection range goes as sigma^(1/4), and 9-16 dB of p90-p10 is a 1.7-2.1x swing in R90 that only one of the two engines can even name.
D_where_this_axis_actually_stands_after_.but_the_real_competitor_is_still_not_pat: it is a published measured sigma table. PathSolver does not enter this axis; our own headline deliberately aspect-averages the lobes away (sigma_robust_summary.paper_ready.recommended_configuration = aspect_avg_anchored), so what the lobes buy is angle-resolved Pd, not the waveform ranking.
